title: YonedaRepo: build together, keep the why
format: Edited current browser captures. Captioned walkthrough without narration; not a continuous recording.

scenes.title: One key opens the prepared workspace
captions: Open yonedarepo.com and choose Have a reviewer access key? The privately supplied key opens a dedicated sandbox.
There is no signup or paid provider-key setup. Codex and Claude connections are already configured on the server.
The key is intentionally absent from this public video. Reviewer access expires and can be revoked by the operator.
You can explore a recorded result immediately. A new prepared trial is optional and has an explicit spending ceiling.

scenes.title: One command, the same prepared example
captions: From the submitted source checkout, run node tools/reviewer.mjs. Node 24 is sufficient; no dependency installation is needed.
The command asks for the same key without echoing it. Credentials never enter command arguments, URLs or source control.
The command opens a checked example immediately. Add --new to approve another two-agent trial; active work resumes without duplication.
One trial runs at a time. Each trial is capped at five dollars within a shared fifty-dollar conservative inference allowance.

scenes.title: Two specialists work concurrently
captions: This is an actual deployed run, not a simulated agent result. Both specialists started from the same canonical base revision.
Codex implements the trail data and filter module. Claude implements an accessible English and Spanish interface.
Their writable paths are disjoint and the shared JavaScript interface is frozen before work begins.
Isolation protects their changes. Scoped MCP tools expose task context, peer status and typed findings without sharing provider credentials.

scenes.title: Recorded activity makes progress visible
captions: Agent activity shows ledger timestamps, elapsed times and the sequence of work, context reads, source capture and checks.
Progress reports describe activity; they do not prove correctness. Technical runtime details remain available behind a disclosure.
You can filter the timeline by agent. An interruption stays visible in history instead of being replaced with a success claim.
Earlier interrupted trials remain recorded. Their conservative usage reservations were retained; the corrected trial is a separate run.

scenes.title: Handoffs are assertions; source capture is evidence
captions: Each specialist publishes a handoff describing the interface and work completed. That message is labelled as an agent assertion.
Trusted capture stops untrusted processes, validates regular files and constructs fresh Git objects in a separate job.
Task cards show the captured revision and changed paths. The integrator waits for both captured specialist outputs.
A digest-bound manifest records which exact task revisions entered assembly. Team integration uses a scoped file overlay.

scenes.title: Review the integrated revision
captions: The final candidate has its own exact captured revision. Review required is displayed above the result and independent checks.
A candidate becoming eligible does not publish it. The canonical published source remains unchanged until a human decision.
Open the diff to inspect the actual captured changes. Large diffs are stored by digest rather than embedded in runtime job bodies.
The preview and checks refer to the captured candidate, while the header identifies the separate canonical published revision.

scenes.title: Independent checks include deployed HTTPS egress
captions: Evaluation runs in a fresh container against the captured revision. The ledger derives the verdict from recorded command exits.
This prepared profile checks an HTML entrypoint, the trail-module interface, bilingual labels and a registry installation.
The registry check executes npm ci against an allowed HTTPS registry. It exercises the deployed container's certificate trust.
These bounded checks provide specific evidence. They are not a claim that every interaction or product requirement is tested.

scenes.title: Inspect the generated product
captions: The preview serves static output from the candidate's recorded manifest on a separate, sandboxed origin.
The two specialist outputs become one bilingual interface consuming the shared trail-data module.
The dataset is explicitly illustrative. The example collects no account identity, location or other personal data.
Previewing a candidate is review evidence. It does not mean that the candidate has been selected or published.

scenes.title: Read the why as a story
captions: Evidence trail is the default context presentation. Intent, contributions, captured source, checks and decision appear as readable stages.
Agent claims stay separate from trusted capture, independent verification and the human shipping decision.
When a decision exists, the trail shows its rationale and each rejected alternative's reason. Missing decisions remain visibly pending.
This provenance is the platform's central contribution: the next agent can recover the reasoning and the evidence that followed it.

scenes.title: Explore a focused graph when needed
captions: Explore graph is optional. Choose a run and inspect a readable neighborhood instead of fitting the entire repository onto one screen.
Select a record to inspect its authority, author, statement and linked evidence. Raw JSON remains an optional diagnostic view.
Context access receipts are written by the adapter. They prove which records were delivered, not that a model understood or used them.
The graph supports exploration; the evidence trail supports ordinary reading. Reviewers can use either without deciphering tiny boxes.

scenes.title: A human decision controls publication
captions: The review dialog asks for a shipping rationale and identifies the checked revision that would be selected.
This walkthrough opens the dialog but submits no decision. The prepared result is left available for the reviewer to decide.
Publication uses an expected-old Git lease, an ancestry check and remote readback. Selected and published remain distinct states.
A failed or conflicting publish can be reconciled with the actual remote HEAD. The failed decision remains recorded in history.

scenes.title: The current prototype and its limits
captions: Cloudflare Workers hosts the platform, Artifacts stores Git, and a transactional repository Durable Object owns authoritative state.
Build together combines scoped specialist work and evidence. Compare mode preserves alternative approaches and the human choice.
Overlapping edits still require a fresh owner-approved run. There is no automatic semantic merge queue or demonstrated large-scale throughput.
Try the current source at github.com/MagnetonIO/yonedarepo and the prepared reviewer workspace at yonedarepo.com.
